cases.sentence: ___ встал на задние лапы и сотворил перед Филиппом Филипповичем какой-то намаз
cases.translation: The dog stood up on his hind legs and performed a kind of bow before Filipp Filippovich.
cases.explain: "Пёс встал" — the dog is the subject of the verb встал, so it stands in the Nominative case.

cases.sentence: Там у братьев пес отведал изолированной ___, а она будет почище извозчичьего кнута
cases.translation: There at the brothers' shop the dog tasted some insulated wire, which turns out to sting worse than a cabman's whip.
cases.explain: The verb «отведал» (he tasted/sampled some of) takes a partitive Genitive object, so проволока becomes проволоки.

cases.sentence: По всей ___ развесили зелено-голубые вывески с надписью «МСПО»
cases.translation: Green-and-blue signs reading 'MSPO' were hung up all over Moscow.
cases.explain: The preposition «по» meaning "all over/throughout" governs the Dative case, so Москва becomes Москве.

cases.sentence: Это вас вселили в ___ Федора Павловича Саблина?
cases.translation: Were you the ones moved into Fyodor Pavlovich Sablin's apartment?
cases.explain: The preposition «в» expressing motion into a place governs the Accusative, so квартира becomes квартиру.

cases.sentence: Перед ___ на стене расправил пушистые усы
cases.translation: In front of the little mirror on the wall he smoothed his bushy mustache.
cases.explain: The preposition «перед» (in front of) governs the Instrumental case, so зеркальце becomes зеркальцем.

cases.sentence: Они оказались в темной ___, которая мгновенно не понравилась псу
cases.translation: They found themselves in a dark little closet, which the dog instantly disliked.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» expressing location (not motion) governs the Prepositional case, so коморка becomes коморке.

reading.ru: Учиться читать совершенно ни к чему, когда мясо и так пахнет за версту.
reading.question: According to the dog's opening reasoning, why is learning to read pointless?
options: Because meat can be smelled from a mile away anyway
Because dogs cannot see letters clearly
Because there are no books worth reading
Because reading takes too much time
reading.correct: Because meat can be smelled from a mile away anyway
reading.explain: The narrator jokes that learning to read is pointless "when meat can be smelled a mile off anyway."

reading.ru: Из сорока тысяч московских псов разве уж какой-нибудь совершенный идиот не сумеет сложить из букв слово «колбаса»?
reading.question: What word does the text say almost any of Moscow's forty thousand dogs could piece together from letters?
reading.correct: Sausage (колбаса)
reading.explain: The text says that out of forty thousand Moscow dogs only a complete idiot couldn't spell out the word "sausage."

reading.ru: Равняясь по голубоватому едкому цвету, шарик, обоняние которого зашиб бензинным дымом мотор, вкатил вместо мясной в магазин электрических принадлежностей братьев Голубизнер на Мясницкой улице.
reading.question: Why did Sharik mistakenly enter the Golubizner brothers' electrical shop instead of a meat shop?
options: He was going by the bluish color of the sign and his sense of smell was dulled by car exhaust
He was chasing another dog and ran in by accident
The shopkeeper called him inside with meat scraps
He was following a policeman's whistle
reading.correct: He was going by the bluish color of the sign and his sense of smell was dulled by car exhaust
reading.explain: Sharik judged shops by their bluish signage, and since car exhaust had dulled his nose, he rolled into the electrical-goods shop by mistake.

reading.ru: Этот знаменитый момент и следует считать началом шариковского образования.
reading.question: What does the narrator say should be considered the start of Sharik's 'education'?
options: The painful moment he bit into the insulated wire at the electrical shop
The day he met Filipp Filippovich
reading.correct: The painful moment he bit into the insulated wire at the electrical shop
reading.explain: The narrator calls the wire-biting incident at the Golubizner shop the famous beginning of Sharik's education.

reading.ru: Изразцовые квадратики, облицовывавшие угловые места в Москве, всегда и неизбежно означали «сыр».
reading.question: What did tiled corner storefronts always mean, according to Sharik's system of reading signs?
reading.correct: Cheese (сыр)
reading.explain: The text states that tiled corner premises in Moscow always and inevitably meant "cheese."

reading.ru: Дверь совершенно бесшумно распахнулась, и молодая красивая женщина в белом фарточке и кружевной наколке предстала перед псом и его господином.
reading.question: Who opened the door when Sharik and his new master arrived at the apartment?
options: A young, pretty woman in a white apron and lace cap
An old man in a fur coat
reading.correct: A young, pretty woman in a white apron and lace cap
reading.explain: The door opened silently and a young, pretty woman in a white apron and lace cap appeared before the dog and his master — this is Zina.

reading.ru: «Пожалуйте, господин Шарик», – иронически пригласил господин.
reading.question: How does the gentleman address Sharik as he invites him inside?
options: He does not speak to the dog at all
reading.correct: Ironically, calling him 'Mr. Sharik'
reading.explain: The gentleman ironically invites him in with the mock-polite address "Пожалуйте, господин Шарик" ("Please, Mr. Sharik").

reading.ru: По снятии шубы он оказался в черном костюме английского сукна, и на животе у него радостно и неярко засверкала золотая цепь.
reading.question: What was revealed once the gentleman took off his fur coat?
options: A black suit of English wool with a gold chain across his stomach
reading.correct: A black suit of English wool with a gold chain across his stomach
reading.explain: Once he removed his fur coat, he appeared in a black suit of English wool, with a gold chain gleaming on his stomach.

reading.ru: Тьма щелкнула и превратилась в ослепительный день.
reading.question: What happened to the dark little room Sharik was led into?
options: The darkness suddenly switched to blinding light
It stayed dark the whole time
It began to smell of sausage
reading.correct: The darkness suddenly switched to blinding light
reading.explain: The text says the darkness 'clicked' and instantly turned into a blinding day — the light being switched on in the examination room.

reading.ru: Пес извернулся, спружинился и вдруг ударил в дверь здоровым боком так, что хряснуло по всей квартире.
reading.question: How did the panicked dog react to being brought into the strange room?
options: He twisted around and slammed his good side into the door so hard it cracked through the whole apartment
He calmly lay down and waited
He ran straight into Zina's arms
reading.correct: He twisted around and slammed his good side into the door so hard it cracked through the whole apartment
reading.explain: Terrified, the dog twisted, coiled, and suddenly struck the door with his good side hard enough that the crash was heard through the whole apartment.

reading.ru: Туча осколков вылетела с громом и звоном, выпрыгнула пузатая банка с рыжей гадостью, которая мгновенно залила весь пол и завоняла.
reading.question: What happened when the dog smashed into the glass in his panic?
options: A cloud of shards flew out along with a jar of foul reddish liquid that spilled and stank
A cat jumped out of the cabinet
The window opened onto the street
reading.correct: A cloud of shards flew out along with a jar of foul reddish liquid that spilled and stank
reading.explain: The impact sent a cloud of glass shards flying along with a pot-bellied jar of foul reddish stuff that flooded the floor and stank.

reading.ru: И тут он окончательно завалился на бок и издох.
reading.question: What does the dog believe happens to him after the chloroform overwhelms him?
options: He finally collapses on his side and dies
He wakes up outside on the street
reading.correct: He finally collapses on his side and dies
reading.explain: Overcome, the dog finally topples over onto his side and, as the text says, 'died' (издох) — though he later revives.

reading.ru: Пес приоткрыл правый томный глаз и краем его увидел, что он туго забинтован поперек боков и живота.
reading.question: What does the dog notice about his own body when he first regains consciousness?
options: He is tightly bandaged across his sides and stomach
He is completely healed with no marks
reading.correct: He is tightly bandaged across his sides and stomach
reading.explain: Opening one languid eye, the dog sees out of the corner of it that he is tightly bandaged across his flanks and belly.

reading.ru: Террор совершенно парализует нервную систему.
reading.question: What claim does Filipp Filippovich make about terror while treating the dog's wound?
options: That terror completely paralyzes the nervous system
That terror is the only cure for animals
That terror has no effect on animals
reading.correct: That terror completely paralyzes the nervous system
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich lectures that terror (as opposed to kindness) completely paralyzes the nervous system.

reading.ru: Мягкие дробные звоночки сыпались в это время по всей квартире, а в отдалении из передней то и дело слышались голоса.
reading.question: What can be heard throughout the apartment as the professor's day of appointments begins?
options: Soft, rapid little bells ringing, and voices from the entryway
reading.correct: Soft, rapid little bells ringing, and voices from the entryway
reading.explain: The text describes soft, rapid little bells ringing all over the apartment while voices are heard from the entrance hall — patients arriving.

reading.ru: Свет заливал целую бездну предметов, из которых самым занятным оказалась громадная сова, сидящая на стене на суку.
reading.question: What object in the professor's study does the dog find most interesting?
options: A huge stuffed owl sitting on a branch on the wall
reading.correct: A huge stuffed owl sitting on a branch on the wall
reading.explain: Among the many objects lit up in the study, the dog finds the enormous owl perched on a branch on the wall the most curious.

reading.ru: На голове у фрукта росли совершенно зеленые волосы, а на затылке они отливали в ржавый табачный цвет.
reading.question: What is strange about the hair of the odd patient who visits the professor?
options: It is green on top and a rusty tobacco color at the back of his head
It is falling out in clumps
It is bright red all over
reading.correct: It is green on top and a rusty tobacco color at the back of his head
reading.explain: The patient's hair had grown completely green on top, while at the back of his head it had a rusty, tobacco-like tint.

reading.ru: Они были кремового цвета, с вышитыми на них шелковыми черными кошками и пахли духами.
reading.question: What is unusual about the patient's underwear (кальсоны) that makes the dog bark?
options: They are cream-colored, embroidered with black silk cats, and scented with perfume
They have holes all over them
reading.correct: They are cream-colored, embroidered with black silk cats, and scented with perfume
reading.explain: The underwear was cream-colored, embroidered with black silk cats, and perfumed — the dog cannot stand the cats and barks.

reading.ru: Наклоняясь, он блестящими глазами исследовал голый живот пациента.
reading.question: What does Filipp Filippovich examine closely on this patient?
reading.correct: The patient's bare stomach
reading.explain: Bending over, Filipp Filippovich examines the patient's bare stomach with keen, shining eyes.

reading.ru: «Я вам, сударыня, ставлю яичники обезьяны», — объявил он и посмотрел строго.
reading.question: What procedure does the professor announce he will perform on the female patient?
reading.correct: Transplanting monkey ovaries into her
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich announces sternly that he is going to implant monkey ovaries in her.

reading.ru: Их было сразу четверо, все молодые люди и все одеты очень скромно.
reading.question: How many visitors arrive from the house committee, and how are they dressed?
options: Four young people, all very modestly dressed
reading.correct: Four young people, all very modestly dressed
reading.explain: The text says there were four of them at once, all young people, all dressed very modestly.

reading.ru: Я — Швондер, она — Вяземская, он — товарищ Пеструхин и Жаровкин.
reading.question: What names does the leader of the group give for himself and his companions?
options: Shvonder, Vyazemskaya, comrade Pestrukhin, and Zharovkin
He refuses to give any names
reading.correct: Shvonder, Vyazemskaya, comrade Pestrukhin, and Zharovkin
reading.explain: The dark-haired leader introduces the group: "I am Shvonder, she is Vyazemskaya, he is comrade Pestrukhin, and Zharovkin."

reading.ru: Я один живу и работаю в семи комнатах
reading.question: How does Filipp Filippovich justify occupying seven rooms by himself?
options: He says he both lives and works alone in all seven rooms
He says the rooms belong to his relatives
He says he is only using one room and renting out the rest
He says the committee gave him permission for eight rooms
reading.correct: He says he both lives and works alone in all seven rooms
reading.explain: Filipp Filippovich answers the committee that he alone lives and works in all seven rooms, and even wants an eighth for a library.

reading.ru: Сейчас ко мне вошли четверо, из них одна женщина, переодетая мужчиной, и двое вооруженных револьверами, и терроризировали меня в квартире с целью отнять часть ее
reading.question: What does Filipp Filippovich tell Pyotr Alexandrovich on the phone about the visitors?
options: That four people, including a woman dressed as a man and two armed with revolvers, came to terrorize him and take part of his apartment
That they came to fix his plumbing
That they brought him a gift
That they wanted to buy his furniture
reading.correct: That four people, including a woman dressed as a man and two armed with revolvers, came to terrorize him and take part of his apartment
reading.explain: On the phone, Filipp Filippovich describes the four visitors, one disguised as a man and two armed with revolvers, terrorizing him to seize part of his flat.

reading.ru: Да, я не люблю пролетариата
reading.question: How does Filipp Filippovich respond when accused of hating the proletariat?
options: He calmly agrees that he does not love the proletariat
reading.correct: He calmly agrees that he does not love the proletariat
reading.explain: When the woman accuses him of hating the proletariat, he sadly but plainly agrees: "Yes, I do not love the proletariat."
